title: Retrieval practice quizzes improve exam performance in introductory biology: a randomized controlled trial
abstract: We randomly assigned 412 students in an introductory biology course to weekly low-stakes retrieval practice quizzes or to re-reading the same material. On the cumulative final exam, students in the quiz condition scored 8.4 percentage points higher than the re-reading group (d = 0.52). The benefit was largest for questions on material covered early in the semester.

passages.text: Participants were 412 undergraduates enrolled in two sections of introductory biology. Students were randomly assigned at the individual level to weekly retrieval practice quizzes or to a re-reading control.
Students in the retrieval practice condition scored 8.4 percentage points higher on the cumulative final exam than students in the re-reading condition (d = 0.52, p < .001).
The advantage of retrieval practice was largest for material from the first third of the semester, consistent with a benefit for long-term retention.

title: Low-stakes weekly quizzing and long-term retention in undergraduate physics
abstract: In a crossover design across two sections of an algebra-based physics course (n = 236), topics practiced with weekly low-stakes quizzes were retained better on a delayed test given eight weeks later than topics practiced with worked-example review (61% vs. 52% correct). Immediate post-unit scores did not differ between conditions.

passages.text: Two sections of algebra-based physics (n = 236) alternated between weekly quizzing and worked-example review across units in a counterbalanced crossover design.
On a delayed test eight weeks later, quizzed topics were answered correctly 61% of the time compared with 52% for review topics. Immediate post-unit scores did not differ.

title: Spaced retrieval practice in a large-enrollment general chemistry course: a quasi-experimental study
abstract: We compared two cohorts of a large general chemistry course (n = 980). The later cohort completed spaced online retrieval practice assignments while the earlier cohort completed massed homework covering the same content. The spaced retrieval cohort scored higher on the common final exam (72.1% vs. 67.5%) and had a lower failure rate (14% vs. 19%).

passages.text: Cohort 1 (fall, n = 472) completed massed weekly homework. Cohort 2 (following fall, n = 508) completed spaced online retrieval practice covering the same content. Both cohorts took a common final exam.
Mean final exam score was 72.1% in the spaced retrieval cohort and 67.5% in the massed homework cohort. The DFW rate fell from 19% to 14%.
Because cohorts were not randomly assigned, differences in student preparation between years cannot be ruled out.

title: The testing effect in undergraduate engineering statics: a randomized classroom experiment
abstract: Engineering students (n = 158) in a statics course were randomly assigned to complete either retrieval practice problem sets without notes or the same problems as open-book study exercises. Retrieval practice improved performance on the unit exams by 6.1 percentage points and on a transfer problem set by 9.3 points.

passages.text: 158 second-year engineering students in a statics course were randomly assigned to closed-book retrieval practice problem sets or the same problems completed open-book.
Retrieval practice improved unit exam performance by 6.1 percentage points and transfer problem performance by 9.3 percentage points relative to open-book study.

title: Online flashcard retrieval practice and final exam scores in undergraduate statistics
abstract: Students in an introductory statistics course (n = 310) could optionally use an online flashcard tool that prompts retrieval of definitions and procedures. After controlling for prior GPA, each additional 100 flashcard retrievals was associated with a 1.9-point higher final exam score. Students who used the tool in the first month benefited most.

passages.text: Usage logs from an optional online flashcard tool were linked to final exam scores for 310 introductory statistics students. Regression models controlled for prior GPA.
Each additional 100 flashcard retrievals was associated with a 1.9-point increase in final exam score after controlling for prior GPA.

title: Retrieval practice quizzes and exam performance in introductory biology
abstract: Preliminary results from an ongoing randomized trial in introductory biology (n = 205, one section). Students assigned to weekly retrieval practice quizzes scored 11.2 percentage points higher on the final exam than students who re-read the material.

passages.text: In this interim analysis of one course section (n = 205), the quiz group scored 11.2 percentage points higher on the final exam than the re-reading group.
These are preliminary results; the full trial across two sections is ongoing.

title: Daily retrieval practice doubles exam scores in undergraduate calculus
abstract: In a study of 640 calculus students, daily retrieval practice was associated with final exam scores roughly twice as high as those of a comparison group (mean 81% vs. 40%). Effects were consistent across all instructors and student subgroups.

passages.text: Students completing daily retrieval practice averaged 81% on the final exam compared with 40% in the comparison group.
This article has been retracted at the request of the journal after an investigation found that the exam data could not be verified.

title: The testing effect in college classrooms: a meta-analysis
abstract: We meta-analyzed 118 effect sizes from classroom studies of retrieval practice in higher education. Retrieval practice produced a moderate overall benefit on course assessments (g = 0.47). Effects were larger when feedback was given and when the final test was delayed.

passages.text: Across 118 effect sizes from higher-education classrooms, the mean effect of retrieval practice on course assessments was g = 0.47 (95% CI 0.40-0.54).
Effects were larger when quizzes included corrective feedback and when the criterial test was delayed by more than a week.

title: Retrieval practice in middle school science classrooms
abstract: Seventh- and eighth-grade science students (n = 540) completed clicker-based retrieval practice at the start of each lesson. Unit test scores were 7 percentage points higher for quizzed than for non-quizzed content.

passages.text: 540 students in grades 7-8 answered clicker retrieval questions at the start of each science lesson for one school year.
Unit test scores were 7 percentage points higher for quizzed content than for non-quizzed content.

title: Simulation-based retrieval practice for procedural skills in medical residents
abstract: Internal medicine residents (n = 64) practiced central line insertion either with repeated simulation-based retrieval of the procedure steps or with video review. Retrieval practice improved checklist scores at a six-month follow-up.

passages.text: 64 internal medicine residents were randomized to simulation-based retrieval practice of central line insertion steps or to video review.
At six-month follow-up, the retrieval practice group scored higher on the procedural checklist (88% vs. 76%).
